Why this addresses the actual failure: the only demonstrated failure is the duplicate "do" key, which is a serialization bug. The repair makes the document valid JSON so evaluation can begin, and the capacity fix removes the second, independent execution error that would surface next. Neither change alters the mechanism, so the prose's claims remain testable rather than replaced.

Preserved previously successful behavior: structural deduplication of repeated deliveries contributes once; the greatest integer revision is authoritative and replaces all lower revisions regardless of delivery order; a latest release contributes 0; an expired latest hold contributes 0 and does not resurrect an older hold; per-item reserved is the sum of active latest quantities; every stock item appears in ascending name order; available = capacity - reserved may be negative (no clamping, no discard, no invented rejection order).

Assumptions: revision, quantity, capacity, expires_at, now are integers; each booking maps to exactly one item; events name listed stock items; a booking/revision pair never carries conflicting contents. Falsifiers: if any two delivered records with equal booking and revision differed in content, the max_by tie-break (first wins) would silently pick one — that would defeat the account; if a booking named an unlisted item, the item row set would be incomplete; if a release could carry a lower revision than a later hold, latest-wins would misclassify. None of these are granted by the task, but they mark the account's boundary. Discriminating case: booking b, rev 1 hold qty 5 expires_at 20, rev 2 hold qty 2 expires_at 5, now=10, capacity 10 — delivery-order or incremental-delta readings give 5 or 7 reserved; the intended account gives reserved 0, available 10. Any future revision must preserve greatest-revision authority and once-only contribution of a duplicated immutable record.",

You fill one artifact. Return JSON only, carrying "body" and "commitments", both strings. "body" is what you have to say. "commitments" is what you are committing to if it is taken up. If evidence blocks are listed, you may add "citations": each names a block id and quotes that block's own words exactly.
Return one JSON object conforming to: {"properties": {"about": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "answers": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "body": {"type": "string"}, "citations": {"items": {"properties": {"block": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}, "quote": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}}, "required": ["block", "quote"], "type": "object"}, "type": "array"}, "commitments": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["body", "commitments"], "type": "object"}

# Return a completed revision

Return the complete executable program in commitments and its explanatory account in body. Resolve the criticism by a causal repair, or retain the candidate if the criticism fails. State the operative change, why it addresses the actual failure, and which previously successful behavior is preserved. You may criticize the task interpretation or checker without being required to agree with them.

## The problem (problem)
Build an executable account of a replicated stock-reservation snapshot.
Deliveries are an unordered bag of immutable event records. The same record may be delivered
many times. Each booking has exactly one immutable item. For each booking, a strictly higher
integer revision replaces ALL lower revisions. A booking/revision pair never has conflicting
contents. The latest revision may be a hold or release. A latest hold is active exactly when
expires_at > input.now; a latest release reserves zero. An expired latest hold does NOT make an
older unexpired hold reappear. Revision order, not delivery order, determines the latest event.
Quantity is the total quantity of that booking version, never an incremental delta.
Stock is input.stock, a list of {item, capacity}; item names are unique. Events only name
listed stock items. Produce a list in ascending item-name order, including items with no events:
[{"item":NAME,"reserved":TOTAL_ACTIVE_LATEST_QUANTITY,"available":CAPACITY-TOTAL},...].
Oversubscription must be visible as negative availability; never clamp, invent rejection order,
or silently discard a booking. Capacity, quantities, revisions, and logical times are integers.
The task is to derive one general procedure from these obligations, not memorize examples.
Explain why replay, reordering, expiry, and later cancellation interact correctly. State what
would falsify your account and which previously successful behavior a revision preserves.

Write a JSON expression program in the commitments string, optionally wrapped as
{"program": EXPR}. The body is unrestricted prose: explain the mechanism, assumptions,
which observations would defeat it, and what successful behavior a change must preserve.
An expression is a JSON literal (numbers, strings, booleans, null, lists), {"var":"name"},
or an operation object. Literal dictionaries use {"op":"object","fields":{"key":EXPR}}.
Input is {"var":"input"}. The available operations and exact fields are:
get: value EXPR, key EXPR, optional default EXPR (missing keys otherwise fail).
if: test EXPR, then EXPR, else EXPR (only selected branch evaluates).
let: name STRING, value EXPR, do EXPR (lexical scope).
map/filter: items EXPR, as STRING, do EXPR (filter do is boolean).
flatmap: same fields; do returns a list; concatenate the lists.
unique: items EXPR (first occurrence order; values compared structurally).
sort: items EXPR (ascending numbers or strings).
max_by/min_by: items EXPR, as STRING, key EXPR (first tie wins; empty fails).
sum/len/not: value EXPR. sum takes a list of numbers; len a list/string/dictionary.
add/sub/mul/eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/and/or/in: args [EXPR, EXPR]. Arithmetic takes numbers
only (never booleans, strings, or lists). Boolean operations and if require booleans.
and/or short circuit. Output values must match the task's declared JSON types exactly.
list: items [EXPR,...] (ordinary JSON lists also evaluate their elements).
Every field is exact: no Python, string interpolation, implicit lambdas, or unknown operators.
Programs are limited to 30,000 expression/collection work units, 100 nesting levels,
4,000 syntax nodes, 4,096 items per collection, 256-bit integers and finite floats,
and 20,000 expanded output nodes. Errors are
execution failures, not refutations of prose. Do not encode the supplied examples as a lookup.

## Candidate and operative program (candidate)
[a2c00800dc3acaa7] (minireason.proposal.v1)
The obligations define a fold over an unordered, duplicating delivery stream whose final state depends only on booking identity, revision, and time. The mechanism is: (1) deduplicate deliveries structurally, because identical immutable records carry no new information; (2) group by booking; (3) within each booking choose the greatest revision, breaking no ties because a booking/revision pair never conflicts; (4) classify only that latest revision: a release contributes 0, a hold contributes quantity only if expires_at > now, otherwise 0; (5) sum those contributions per item; (6) emit every stock row sorted by item, with available = capacity - reserved, allowing negative availability. Replay and reordering are harmless because the result is a function of the set of (booking, revision) records, not their delivery order; duplicate delivery is absorbed by structural deduplication. Expiry is a predicate on the latest revision's expires_at against input.now, so an expired hold vanishes entirely and cannot resurrect an older hold. Later cancellation works because a release is a strictly higher integer revision for the same booking, so it replaces all lower holds and contributes zero. Oversubscription is never clamped or filtered: reserved can exceed capacity and available becomes negative, which is the observable signal. The procedure assumes revision numbers are comparable integers, each booking has exactly one item, events name listed stock items, and no booking/revision pair carries contradictory content; an event for an unlisted item would make the account incomplete rather than falsify it, since the task guarantees events name listed items. A discriminating failure case is: booking b has revision 1 hold quantity 5 expires_at 20 and revision 2 hold quantity 2 expires_at 5, with now=10 and capacity 10. A delivery-order or incremental-delta implementation might count 5 or 5+2; the correct account discards revision 1, sees the latest hold expired, reserves 0, and reports available 10. Any revision of this program must preserve that the latest revision by integer order is authoritative and that duplicate delivery of the same record contributes once. The program is a direct expression of these steps using group-like selection via max_by, so it is not a lookup of the public examples.

## Criticism and its grounds (criticism)
[9bf41f296509bd35] (minireason.criticism.v1)
I inspect the program, the prose, and the execution evidence separately, and the evidence here is not evidence about the account at all.

The only recorded observation is an interpreter-level failure: PROGRAM_NOT_JSON: duplicate key: do. That is a construction/translation failure, not a refutation of the prose. The JSON object handed to the evaluator has a duplicated "do" key, which most JSON parsers reject before any expression is ever evaluated. So no case actually runs, no distinguishing input is exercised, and the failure tells us nothing about whether the mechanism is correct. Per the ground rules, an interpreter error is a construction or translation failure, and I must not treat it as proof the prose account is false.

Looking past the malformed wire encoding at the mechanism the prose describes, I can identify where a real defect would live if one existed, and whether the intended program has one. The intended algorithm is: deduplicate structurually, group by booking, take max_by revision, keep only latest holds with expires_at > now, sum quantities per item, emit every stock row sorted by item with available = capacity - reserved. That is the right shape for the obligations. Duplicate delivery is absorbed by unique; revision order, not arrival order, decides the latest event; expiry is a predicate on the latest record only, so an expired latest hold cannot resurrect an older hold; a later release is a strictly higher revision and replaces all lower ones with zero contribution; oversubscription is left unclamped so available can go negative.

So: no demonstrated defect in the account. What is demonstrated is a broken delivery of the program. The critic's honest verdict is unresolved, not refuted — the evidence is blocked at parse time.

The smallest distinguishing case to check once the encoding is fixed is the one the prose itself names: booking b, revision 1 hold quantity 5 expires_at 20, revision 2 hold quantity 2 expires_at 5, now=10, capacity 10. A delivery-order or incremental-delta reading gives reserved 5 or 7; the correct account discards revision 1, finds the latest hold expired, reserves 0, and reports available 10. That case separates the intended mechanism from the two most common misreadings.

Cause of the observed failure: the serialized expression object contains two sibling "do" keys under the same node, so the document is not valid JSON and evaluation never starts. It is a packaging bug, not a semantic one. I cannot certify the program runs correctly until it parses; I also cannot say it is false.
commitments: I will not treat the PROGRAM_NOT_JSON error as a refutation of the prose. I will report the mechanism's status as unresolved at the execution layer — the candidate never ran — while saying plainly that the described procedure, if encoded legally, implements the required obligations: structural dedup of deliveries, grouping by booking, selection of the greatest revision, expiry evaluated only on the latest record, zero contribution from releases and from expired latest holds, per-item summation, and unclamped available = capacity - reserved. I will name the duplicate "do" key in the serialized expression object as the cause of the parse failure and identify it as a construction/translation defect, not a semantic one. I will not invent a fault in the logic. I will name the discriminating case booking b, rev 1 hold qty 5 expires_at 20, rev 2 hold qty 2 expires_at 5, now=10, capacity 10, as the test that separates the intended account from delivery-order and incremental-delta misreadings, and I will require the program to be re-encoded as valid JSON before any correctness verdict is given.
